source.version: PsyArXiv preprint downloaded from OSF (DOI 10.31234/osf.io/5tfng; search record lists v1, first posted 2026-06-15). The document itself shows no date or version label. Main text (18 pages, line-numbered) followed by a 52-page Supplementary Information.
source.title_on_document: The value of generative AI in creative teams depends on when it enters collective search

supplement.where: Supplementary Information appended to the main text (PDF pp. 19-70, numbered SI pp. 1-52). SI p. 8 (PDF p. 26) also refers to 'submitted supplementary files' with the AI-scoring code, and SI p. 4 (PDF p. 22) to 'code documentation' for the AI assistant's role prompt; neither is in this PDF. Data and code at https://osf.io/eapdn.
supplement.holds: All tables with numbers: arm Ns and creativity means (SD) (Supp. Table 1), sample flow (Table 2), planned contrasts with mean differences, 95% CIs, Hedges g and p (Tables 5-7), timing-factor regressions with HC3 SEs (Tables 8-10, 16, 22), rater reliability (Table 11), robustness (Tables 13-14), process measures by condition (Table 15). The main text gives only g and p for the headline contrasts. The AI assistant's role prompt and the AI-rater scoring code sit outside this PDF.

paper_design_summary: In a lab experiment, 444 participants (who logged in with student IDs) worked in 148 three-person teams on a 40-minute online product-design task (15 min divergent ideation, 15 min convergent selection, 10 min final review). Teams were randomly assigned to one of five AI-access regimes: an integrated DeepSeek V3.2 assistant in Stage 1 only (C1), Stage 2 only (C2), all stages (C3), no AI (C4), or Stage 1 plus a persistent warning (C5). Four human raters scored each team's final proposal document blind to condition on originality, appropriateness, elaboration and text quality, combined into a creativity composite. Ten LLM raters scored the same proposals as a diagnostic.

studies.label: Phase-contingent AI team experiment (product design, 5 conditions x 3 tasks)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Team-level AI-access regime (C1 Stage-1 AI, C2 Stage-2 AI, C3 full-process AI, C4 no AI, C5 Stage-1 AI plus warning), crossed with one of three product-design tasks. 150 sessions (10 per condition-by-task cell) were put in a randomized sequence, and randomly formed three-person teams were allocated to sessions in that sequence.
assignment.quote: Based on the 5 (conditions) x 3 (tasks) design, we generated 150 experimental sessions (10 sessions per combination, e.g., C1T1, C1T2...). The sequence of these 150 sessions was fully randomized. Participants were randomly formed into teams of three

arms.description: No LLM interface at any stage (control).

arms.name: C1 Divergent AI
arms.description: Integrated LLM assistant available during Stage 1 (15-min divergent ideation) only.

arms.name: C2 Convergent AI
arms.description: Integrated LLM assistant available during Stage 2 (15-min convergent selection) only.

participants.exclusions: The paper does not give a people count at assignment. 150 sessions were generated (planned 150 teams). A system setup error created an extra C1T1 session and omitted a C1T3 session, and two sessions were removed for invalid data, leaving 148 analytic teams (C1 30, C2 30, C3 30, C4 29, C5 29) and 444 participants. Supp. Table 2 reports 0 exclusions after the analytic-file stage. Team counts per arm: Supp. Table 1 and Supp. Fig. 1b.
participants.who: Participants who logged in with student IDs; three-person teams in a controlled computer laboratory; base fee 45 RMB plus up to 50 RMB bonus for top-10 teams. Balance covariates include grade and discipline.
participants.country: not_stated (instructions translated from Chinese, payment in RMB, IRB approval of the Chinese Academy of Sciences)
participants.quote: The analytic file set contains 444 survey respondents, 148 rated analytic teams, and 148 matched final proposal documents.
participants.locator: SI p. 4 (PDF p. 22), S1.1-S1.2; Supp. Table 1, SI p. 9 (PDF p. 27); Supp. Table 2, SI p. 10 (PDF p. 28); abstract p. 1

ai_tool.name_model: DeepSeek V3.2 via API, temperature 0.1, assigned a specific role (prompt in code documentation, not in this PDF)
ai_tool.how_used: An LLM chat panel inside the team workspace. Each member could query it independently during the enabled stage(s). Team chat was also streamed to the AI in real time. A new API session was started for each group. The interface was greyed out in disabled stages and absent in C4.

task.description: Team product-design task that combines two distant objects (T1 backpack + pet accessory, T2 refrigerator + calendar, T3 shoes + map). Each team submitted one final proposal (product name, feature list, description, 250-word limit), which could contain several proposal concepts. The task is a written product concept (it could also be coded idea_generation).
task.duration: 40 minutes: 15 min divergent search, 15 min convergent selection, 10 min final review and submission

outcomes.name: Human-rated creativity composite (calibrated team-level creativity score, cs_adj_mean)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Four raters (described as experts, blind to condition) scored every proposal in each team's document. Creativity = 0.70 x Originality + 0.15 x Appropriateness + 0.15 x Elaboration, where Originality = 0.9 x Quality (1-7) + 0.1 x Quantity (feature count mapped to 1-7) + naming bonus. Averaged across proposals within a team and then across the four raters, with rater-severity (MFRM-equivalent) calibration. ICC(2,k) = 0.421. Robustness: leave-one-rater-out, expert-only, mixed model, bootstrap (Supp. Table 13), task-specific contrasts (Supp. Table 14), and a timing-factor OLS with task fixed effects and HC3 SEs (Supp. Table 8: Stage-1 AI b = 0.491, HC3 SE 0.152, 95% CI [0.194, 0.788], p = 0.0012; Stage-2 AI b = 0.151, SE 0.166, p = 0.365; full-process increment -0.187, p = 0.384; warning increment -0.214, p = 0.176; N = 148).

contrasts.reported: C3 4.81 (SD 0.52, 30 teams, 90 participants) vs C4 4.35 (SD 0.67, 29 teams, 87 participants); mean difference 0.465 [0.160, 0.770]; Hedges g = 0.77 [0.24, 1.30]; p = 0.00424 (Welch-style)

outcomes.name: Originality composite (originality_total_mean)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 0.9 x originality-quality rating (1-7) + 0.1 x originality-quantity (deduplicated valid-feature count mapped to 1-7) + naming novelty bonus (0, 0.5 or 1); team mean across proposals and raters. outcomes.name: Originality-quality rating ('Quality', quality_mean)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 rating of how novel, surprising and non-obvious the concept is (labelled 'Quality' in the tables; the paper says the quality panel refers to the originality-quality rating). ICC(2,k) = 0.372. Timing model (Supp. Table 9): Stage-1 AI b = 0.521, HC3 SE 0.165, p = 0.00162; Stage-2 AI b = 0.159, p = 0.355.

outcomes.name: Appropriateness (appropriateness_mean)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 rating of usefulness, feasibility and plausible user need. ICC(2,k) = 0.349. Timing model (Supp. Table 9): Stage-1 AI b = 0.549, HC3 SE 0.137, p = 5.9e-05; Stage-2 AI b = 0.219, p = 0.106; warning increment -0.329, p = 0.0245 (Supp. Table 10).

outcomes.name: Elaboration (elaboration_mean)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 rating of detail and development of the proposal. ICC(2,k) = 0.512. Timing model (Supp. Table 9): Stage-1 AI b = 0.859, HC3 SE 0.164; Stage-2 AI b = 0.377, SE 0.176, p = 0.0318; full-process increment -0.582, p = 0.0247; warning increment -0.453, p = 0.0176 (Supp. Table 10).

outcomes.name: Text quality (text_quality_mean, supplementary indicator, not in composite)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 rating of whether the text is clearly categorized, readable and logically coherent (writing quality, not creativity). ICC(2,k) = 0.384. Timing model (Supp. Table 9): Stage-1 AI b = 0.604, HC3 SE 0.157, p = 0.000118; Stage-2 AI b = 0.120, p = 0.396.

outcomes.name: AI-rated creativity (pooled z-score of ten LLM raters, ai_pool_z_all10)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Ten LLM raters (Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek V3, DeepSeek V4 pro, Gemini 3.1 flash, Gemini 3.1 pro, GPT 5.5, GPT 5.5 pro, Kimi K2.6) scored the proposals; the paper uses them only as a diagnostic layer. Pooled ICC(2,k) = 0.853; proposal-level correlation with human ratings r = 0.20 to 0.39 (Supp. Tables 24-25). Only timing-model coefficients are printed. Supp. Fig. 10b shows Hedges g by contrast with one model family left out (figure only).

outcomes.name: Alpha diversity (within-team semantic breadth of the final proposal document)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean pairwise TF-IDF distance among paragraph-level idea units within one team's final proposal document. It measures variety within one team's own output, not similarity across teams, so it is coded flexibility, not diversity. The paper treats it as a mechanism variable. Means (SD) by condition: C4 0.916 (0.038), C1 0.950 (0.019), C2 0.948 (0.026), C3 0.954 (0.020), C5 0.946 (0.024) (Supp. Table 15).

company_involvement.description: All authors are at the Chinese Academy of Sciences or Zhejiang University. The paper says the best proposals 'might be recommended to industry partners' (SI p. 3, PDF p. 21); no company funded or ran the study according to the document.

eligibility.reason: Teams were randomly assigned to AI-access regimes, including a no-AI control (SI p. 3, PDF p. 21; main text p. 3). 444 people were analyzed across all five arms (C3 vs C4 alone: 90 + 87 = 177 people). The primary outcome is a blind human rating of the team's final proposal (Supp. Table 5). Assignment and analysis are at the team level (148 teams), so the effective number of independent units is 148 teams, not 444 people.

one_line_finding: Compared with no AI, full-process AI raised the human-rated creativity of team proposals (4.81 vs 4.35, Hedges g = 0.77, p = 0.004), as did divergent-stage-only AI (g = 0.81, p = 0.003), while convergent-stage-only AI (g = 0.25, p = 0.328) and divergent AI with a warning (g = 0.43, p = 0.104) did not (Supp. Table 5, PDF p. 31).
open_questions: Question code: in C1 and C5 the AI was available only in Stage 1, and the final proposal was written in Stage 3 without AI, but the scored output is the product of the whole 40-minute session that included AI-assisted ideation. I coded all outcomes with_ai with ai_available_when_produced = 'mixed'; a reviewer may prefer a different code for the stage-restricted arms.

Unit of assignment and analysis is the three-person team (148 teams); people counts (444) meet the 50-person rule, but standard errors are team-level HC3 or Welch tests over teams. Extraction should use n = teams for SE(d).

Rater independence: two of the four human raters in Supp. Table 11 are listed as 'YU' and 'ZHOU', which match two author surnames (Shumin Yu, Weihua Zhou). The paper does not say who the raters were, only that rating was blind to condition. Supp. Table 13 also reports an 'expert-only' robustness check, which suggests not all four raters were experts, although SI p. 6 says submissions were 'forwarded to four experts'.
Primary record choice: under codebook rule 3, C3 (full-process AI) is the arm closest to free chatbot use. The paper's own headline contrast is C1 vs C4.
No across-team diversity (homogenization) outcome is reported; alpha diversity is within-team breadth.

Small inconsistencies: Supp. Fig. 5 caption gives C1-C4 g = 0.80 and C2-C4 p = 0.34 and C5-C4 g = 0.42, p = 0.11, while Supp. Table 5 gives g = 0.81, p = 0.328 and g = 0.43, p = 0.104. The C5 calibrated mean is 4.643 vs a raw mean of 4.653 (Supp. Table 12).
notes: Outcomes not listed because they are not creativity or diversity scores of the output: semantic proximity of final proposals to AI outputs (Supp. Tables 20-22, AI-use teams only, n = 118), Stage-1 chat characters and other process measures (Supp. Tables 15-18), AI-human rating divergence (Supp. Table 26), and moderator screens (Supp. Table 19). Task-specific C1-C4 and C3-C4 contrasts (Supp. Table 14, PDF p. 40) and robustness checks (Supp. Table 13, PDF p. 39: expert-only g = 0.926 for C1-C4 and 0.836 for C3-C4; mixed model b = 0.507 and 0.453, p < 0.001) are variants of S1-O1. The markdown conversion drops the first sentence of the abstract and part of SI S1.1; all numbers above were checked against the PDF pages cited. PDF pages 19-70 are SI pages 1-52 (SI page = PDF page minus 18). Final proposal length in characters is reported only descriptively (Supp. Table 15, PDF p. 41: C4 442.2, C1 665.8, C2 753.7, C3 705.7, C5 574.0; no test) and is not listed as an outcome because no measure code fits a character count.
